content.text: {"relation": "REFINED", "consensus_summary": "The net primarily symbolizes the gospel/kingdom of God gathering people through evangelism ('fishers of men,' dragnet parable), with widely acknowledged secondary senses: a snare set by the wicked, and God's net of judgment over nations; minority readings include predatory empire (Habakkuk 1) and the unbroken net as church unity.", "book_summary": "The net is any power's enclosure that takes the living from the sea of peoples 'of every kind, alive' for the sorting of a harvest whose catch is never ransomed—wholly consecrated or wholly destroyed (linking the Hebrew word for dragnet with the 'devoted thing,' cherem). Instances: armies are God's net carrying nations to judgment; the gospel is the kingdom's net; the wicked hide theirs and are caught in it themselves.", "consensus_core_identification": "Net = the gospel/kingdom's instrument for gathering souls (evangelism), with sorting at final judgment; secondarily a snare of the wicked or God's instrument of judgment.", "book_core_identification": "Net = the generic enclosure by which a power gathers the living from the sea of peoples for a total, unransomable sorting (consecration or destruction); the gospel-net, God's army-net, and the wicked's snare are all species of this one function.", "core_relation": "BOOK_BROADENS", "extension_relation": "PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION", "boundary_disagreement": "The consensus treats the evangelistic gospel-net as the primary meaning and the judgment/snare nets as separate secondary senses. The book abstracts a single unifying definition that covers all three, elevating armies-as-God's-net (Ezek 32:3; 17:20; Hab 1) to co-equal status with the gospel-net, and reclassifies the evangelistic gathering itself as intrinsically a gathering-unto-sorting whose catch is 'never ransomed'—vessels or furnace—rather than a primarily positive image of soul-winning. It also adds the cherem (devoted-thing) dimension of total consecration/destruction, which no consensus response mentions.", "material_contradiction": "", "rationale": "The book retains the consensus's central referents—the gospel as the kingdom's net (Matt 13:47-50) and God's judgment net over nations—so there is no replacement of the identification. But it materially changes the framing and boundary: instead of evangelism as the primary sense with judgment as a distinct alternative, all nets share one core function (enclosure of the living for irrevocable sorting), and the emphasis shifts from gathering-in to the herem-like finality of the catch. This is a real boundary and emphasis disagreement (broadening plus reclassification of the positive evangelistic sense), not mere wording, and not a contradiction of the consensus referent, so REFINED fits.", "citation_support": "PARTIAL", "strongest_objection": "One could argue MATCH: every element of the book's entry (gospel-net, God's judgment-net via armies, the wicked's self-ensnaring net, gathering of every kind with final sorting) appears somewhere across the consensus responses' primary meaning and alternatives, so the book merely synthesizes what the consensus already lists rather than changing any extension. The rebuttal is that the book's unifying 'never ransomed' cherem thesis and its subordination of evangelism to a judgment-harvest function materially alter the primary identification's character and boundaries, and the cherem/devoted-thing claim is unsupported by the printed citations alone.", "confidence": "medium"}
